messages:
Sam: heads-up — infra-bot alert for apac-gpu-pool0: ECC correctable spike, ~5.4x baseline over the last 10m. seeing increasing Xid 13/61 on a few nodes. anyone oncall? :eyes:

infra-bot: [ALERT] ECC_CORRECTABLE_RATE_HIGH apac-gpu-pool0 10m_avg=5.4x threshold=3.0x -> fired 2312345678

Maria: on it, pulling dashboards. which exact nodes are noisy? apac-gpu-pool0, right?

Sam: yes — noisy hosts: gpu-node-02, gpu-node-05, gpu-node-07. latency for small-gen models up ~12% p50, some job retries/ooms. logs show repeated Xid 13 and NVML resets on gpu-node-02.

Jordan: can we avoid a full drain? Last time a blanket drain caused regional capacity pressure and customer impact. Suggest soft-quarantine: block new allocations + migrate long-running jobs off the affected hosts.

Lee: +1 to soft-quarantine. Also recommend running nvml diag + a short memtest on suspect cards overnight. Before that, verify there's no driver/kernel rollout that caused regressions. ops-bot any recent infra changes in APAC?

ops-bot: No kernel/driver updates applied in apac in the last 24h. No orchestration changes flagged.

Maria: grabbing samples from node via nvidia-smi and ECC counters. quick sample: `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC | grep -i "Correctable"` shows elevated counts on GPU2 and GPU5. excerpt:
``nGPU 2: Correctable ECC errors: 1320 (last 1h)
GPU 5: Correctable ECC errors: 1108 (last 1h)
``

Sam: can we correlate with rack power/thermal? metrics show temps stable, fans OK. power draw looks nominal.

Jordan: decision proposal (for quick sync):
1) apply pool-level soft-quarantine (no new pods scheduled on affected nodes)
2) migrate evictible/stateful jobs gracefully with 5m grace
3) schedule probe + memtest overnight on suspect cards
4) if errors double or we see Xid -> uncorrectable in next 30m, escalate to full auto-drain and card replace.

Lee: what's our current auto-drain trigger? I recall it's 3x baseline sustained for 30m + Xid growth and reboots. For small APAC pools might want a pool-specific sensitivity.

Maria: lowering global thresholds is risky. propose a pool override: apac-gpu-pool0 sensitivity=high -> trigger at 2.5x sustained for 15m. keeps global defaults intact.

Sam: ops playbook: @Maria apply soft-quarantine label `node.kubernetes.io/quarantine=apac-ecc-2312`; @Jordan start migrations; @Lee arrange memtest and pull spare cards if memtest fails. Create incident INF-2312 to track.

Maria: applied labels -> `kubectl label nodes gpu-node-02 gpu-node-05 node.kubernetes.io/quarantine=apac-ecc-2312` and cordoned for new scheduling. confirmed no new pods scheduled. :white_check_mark:

Jordan: starting evictions with `kubectl drain gpu-node-02 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300` and same for gpu-node-05. migrating 12 pods total, 3 critical pods requeued to other regions as fallback.

ops-bot: Migration started: 12 pods evicted, 3 pods requeued across regions. note: cross-region fallback will incur egress and standby capacity cost. estimated incremental cost for next 24h: ~$600.

Sam: monitoring window 30m. if corrected ECC errors double or Xid counts escalate to uncorrectable -> full drain + replace. record decision.

Lee: also let's deploy a lightweight probe on the nodes that writes NVML counters every 5m and runs a small mem-load pattern to try to reproduce. write logs to `/var/log/apac-ecc-probe.log`.

Maria: probe job scheduled (k8s cronjob), collecting 5m cadence samples.

infra-bot: [UPDATE 2312345900] apac-gpu-pool0 corrected rate dropped to 1.8x after migrations; Xid counts stable; no reboots observed in the last 20m.

Sam: good sign. keep watch for 2h and then we can clear quarantine. action items: add pool sensitivity configs, expand probe to other small pools, document memtest results in INF-2312.

Jordan: quick note on automation: we should add an adaptive policy that considers pool capacity headroom before auto-drain triggers (if pool available capacity < 15% raise sensitivity). avoids noisy drains in tight pools.

Lee: agree. also add a flag to auto-drain decisions to prefer hot-swap replacement vs rack-level drain when card-level failures detected (avoid moving all workloads).

Sam: thanks all. keeping thread open. will close incident if stable for 2h. :wave:
